title: Cross-platform play: inside or outside this multiplayer increment?
summary: The Objective leaves cross-platform support genuinely undecided, and the Definition deliberately carries that openness — no non-goal, no constraint, only a neutral, reversible preference against transport/serialization choices that would make either answer more expensive later. Only you can set this boundary edge. The decision in your terms: including cross-platform makes it a requirement of this increment — the chosen transport/serialization must actually work on both target platforms and the acceptance surface gains a genuinely cross-platform two-client scenario, growing cost now and coupling to the still-unmeasured latency question (F4). Excluding it keeps the increment the minimal authoritative two-player session (two processes, direct join, localhost/LAN), with the path to a later cross-platform increment preserved only by the current replaceable-transport preference. A third path settles the edge cheaply without claiming the feature: no cross-platform acceptance, but platform-neutrality of the first transport/serialization layer becomes a hard, verifiable constraint rather than a soft preference.

options.label: Exclude — record as a deliberate non-goal
options.description: Cross-platform is recorded as a deliberate non-goal of this increment. The bounded scope stays the minimal two-process authoritative session on localhost/LAN, and reversibility is carried only by the existing preference against transport/serialization choices that would make a later cross-platform increment materially costlier. Cross-platform play is re-opened as its own increment when prioritized.

options.label: Include — add cross-platform as a requirement
options.description: Cross-platform participation becomes a requirement of the bounded scope: the chosen transport/serialization must run on both target platforms, and the acceptance model gains an explicitly cross-platform two-client join-and-propagate scenario. This grows the cost and test surface now and interacts with the still-unmeasured latency question (F4).

options.label: Constrain only — cross-platform-ready groundwork, no cross-platform feature
options.description: A middle path: no cross-platform feature is claimed and no cross-platform acceptance is added, but the current soft preference is elevated to a hard constraint — the first transport/serialization layer must be replaceable/platform-neutral and demonstrably swappable — so the later cross-platform increment stays cheap. Settles the scope edge now without asserting tested cross-platform play.
